preamble: The alveolar lateral approximant [l] shifts to the voiced retroflex flap [ɽ] through place assimilation in South Asian languages, particularly in retroflex harmony environments. This transformation occurs in Tamil and other Dravidian languages where retroflexed consonants trigger retroflex spreading to adjacent segments.

examples.note: Casual speech allophone in retroflex-conditioned contexts

Synchronic allophony: Kanuri /l/ is realized as the retroflex flap [ɽ] before /i/ (/l/ → [ɽ] / _i). Cyffer argues the rule is older than Kanuri consonant weakening, since Kanuri loans in Ngizim, Bade and Karekare reflect it as r (Ngizim zōrí 'fool', Bade rītərîn 'Monday').
Before vowels other than /i/ the lateral stays [l]: lâdə 'Sunday', bígəla 'harvest season'.
